$comment: Frozen cross-package table for the inline-sections match rule. See stories/test-script-sections-contract.md §2. Consumed by the root vitest suite (parser + expander), runner-core's node --test suite, and both extensions' copy-parity tests. Every implementation of matchText() must reproduce BOTH the derived text and the boolean. Do not edit a row to make an implementation pass — the table is the specification.
$deliberatelyAbsent: inline-sections-runtime.md §9 lists 'a formatted call site inside a skill body' among the required rows. It is NOT here and cannot be: a pure text table cannot express which array an implementation read. In a TIGHT markdown list extractPlainText is the identity function, so a `**Login**` row passes whether the implementation reads steps[i] or rawSteps[i]. That hazard is pinned by the contract §2.3 `{{target}}` scenario, asserted through parseTestFile in the root parser/expander suite.
derivation: matchText(s) = casefold(trim(stripLeadingNoHooksMarker(s))), where stripLeadingNoHooksMarker uses /^\[no-hooks\]\s*/i (verbatim from src/parser/markdown.ts) and casefold is String.prototype.toLowerCase() — never toLocaleLowerCase().
inputContract: Both sides arrive already stripped of the `N. ` list prefix and already trimmed. Rows that supply untrimmed input exist only to pin the strip-before-trim ORDER; they cannot occur on a real document.

rows.name: exact
rows.why: Baseline: identical text on both sides.

rows.name: step lowercased
rows.why: Matching is case-insensitive.

rows.name: step uppercased
rows.why: Case-insensitivity is symmetric.

rows.name: heading uppercased
rows.why: The same casefold applies to the map key, not just the step.

rows.name: step has trailing whitespace
rows.why: trim() is part of the derivation.

rows.name: step has leading whitespace
rows.why: trim() covers both ends. The marker strip is a no-op here.

rows.name: name contains spaces
rows.why: Names are matched as whole step text, not tokenized.

rows.name: internal whitespace differs
rows.why: The derivation trims the ends only. Internal runs are NOT collapsed — an implementation that normalizes whitespace fails here.

rows.name: no-hooks marker
rows.why: A [no-hooks]-prefixed call still resolves; the marker's hook-skipping meaning is preserved separately.

rows.name: no-hooks marker uppercased
rows.why: The CLI marker regex carries the /i flag; every reimplementation of the strip must too.

rows.name: no-hooks marker with no separating space
rows.why: The regex trailing \s* matches zero spaces.

rows.name: whitespace before the no-hooks marker defeats the strip
rows.why: Order is strip-then-trim, and the strip is anchored at ^. Cannot occur on a real document (inputs arrive trimmed); pinned so all six implementations agree on the order rather than each picking one.

rows.name: bold step text
rows.why: Match is on RAW text: no markdown-formatting normalization. NOTE this row does NOT discriminate steps[i] from rawSteps[i] — in a tight list extractPlainText returns `**Login**` unchanged, so both readings produce `**login**` and pass. See $deliberatelyAbsent.

rows.name: the heading side uses the same derivation
rows.why: matchText is applied to BOTH sides, so the marker strip runs on the heading too. Without this row an implementation could use plain trim()+toLowerCase() for map keys and pass all other rows. Such a name is refused at parse time ('[' prefix, contract §2.5), so this row pins the derivation only — like the leading-whitespace row above.

rows.name: bold on both sides is byte-equal
rows.why: Confirms the rule is raw equality, not 'formatting is always rejected'.

rows.name: backticked step text
rows.why: Same as bold — codespan is raw text too.

rows.name: trailing period
rows.why: Trailing punctuation is a near-miss, not a call. The authoring diagnostic catches it; the expander does not.

rows.name: turkish dotted capital I lowercases to i + combining dot
rows.why: toLowerCase('İ') is U+0069 U+0307 (two code points). Under toLocaleLowerCase('tr') it would be U+0069 alone and this row would NOT match.

rows.name: turkish dotted capital I does not match plain i
rows.why: The discriminating row: toLocaleLowerCase('tr') WOULD match here. Any implementation returning true is locale-sensitive and will disagree between a Turkish-locale client and a C-locale server.

rows.name: ascii capital I lowercases to plain i
rows.why: The other direction: toLocaleLowerCase('tr') maps ASCII I to U+0131 (dotless) and would NOT match. Together with the row above this pins toLowerCase from both sides.
